headline: BCG | Booth MBA | Financial Literacy
about: I am an experienced strategy consultant and project leader, currently working in the Chicago office of Boston Consulting Group (BCG). Previously, I was a strategy and consulting manager at Accenture, where I spent 5 years. I have experience leading strategy teams, facilitating meetings with senior client executives, and designing complex Excel models and Tableau dashboards to drive powerful insights through data analytics. I also have a full-time MBA (High Honors) from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. I'm an experienced manager of teams as large as 60, and frequently speak to audiences of 250+, bringing energy, humor, and clarity to personal finances. I used to be a freelance journalist and have published more than 200 articles on business, financial literacy, public policy, and education. In my free time, I am the CFO of a nonprofit supporting community development in Kenya.

headline: BCG, MBA’24 @ London Business School
about:
Seasoned Product Manager specialising in the fintech sector, with a rich educational background including an MBA from London Business School and international experience from Chicago Booth School of Business.

Throughout my career, I've focused on bridging the gap between finance and technology, spearheading initiatives that optimise financial operations and enhance customer engagement through data-driven insights and innovative solutions. My work at top-tier consulting companies and financial institutions has enabled me to lead significant projects, from developing state-of-the-art trading and CRM platforms using microservices architecture to implementing strategic API integrations that support hundreds of thousands of clients. I also hold Certified Financial Analyst (CFA) and Financial Risk Manager (FRM) qualifications that underpin my strategic decision-making and risk management capabilities.

Leadership is at the core of my professional ethos. I've managed diverse teams, fostering an environment of innovation and accountability, and driven projects that not only meet but anticipate market needs and challenges. My goal is to continue leveraging my expertise to lead fintech solutions that are not only technologically advanced but also strategically aligned with global financial trends and customer needs.

I am passionate about the transformative power of fintech and am always open to connecting with like-minded professionals and exploring new opportunities to innovate within this exciting field.

experience.description:
Interned in the Tech, Media, and Communication practice, where I played a key role in driving strategic projects including M&A integration, investment proposals, and acquisition target selection for a sovereign wealth fund:

•	Supported the M&A process and planned the integration of companies within the Project Management Office, assessing the premises for revenue synergies and cost synergies of about £600m.
•	Developed investment proposal for 3 acquisition targets in software and cybersecurity sectors with a cumulative value of £340m and long-term synergy generation of £127m
•	Built a screening methodology to come up with 25 new acquisition targets in the government technology market in the U.S., bringing up to £106m of investment opportunities to a fund portfolio pipeline

Directed development of advanced wealth management, analytics, trading, compliance, and CRM modules in microservice architecture, managing a technical team of 9 with a £610k budget:

•	Employed machine learning models in Python to discover uniform trading patterns in historical data and designed a flexible order-clustering algorithm, resulting in £400k cost savings annually
•	Identified and resolved critical discrepancies in trading positions using SQL scripts, crafting a data recovery strategy that minimized downtime and ensured 99% consistency across trading systems.
•	Adapted to evolving communication needs by leading a cross-divisional project to integrate a chat platform into a mobile application, increasing engagement by 30% amid shifting user demands
•	Led integration of strategic API access to the retail brokerage division with 800k clients, communicating technical details to non-technical stakeholders and negotiating service agreement
•	Designed pre-emptive response strategies for customer satisfaction issues by analysing feedback from financial advisors and detecting common patterns, leading to a 4% reduction in churn rate

Performed business analysis at the early stages of a rapidly growing product: web-based software for financial advisors in the stock/bond market:

•	Enhanced investment workflow by automating routine operations through a series of employee interviews across 3 divisions and diagnosing legacy processes, saving £1.1m annually
•	Launched a data-driven wealth management product that secured £30m in assets within the first year by leveraging analytical power of Monte Carlo simulation in the financial planning phase
•	Created and implemented a new regulatory-compliant portfolio risk methodology, customising the exposure calculation algorithm for efficient execution time and freeing £36m of invested assets

Responsible for the full cycle of credit risk management in the corporate & investment banking division: methodology, modeling, testing and reporting, as well as day-to-day management of risk exposure.

•	Prepared risk analytics reports for bank management and the Board of Directors by coordinating with multiple divisions, bi-weekly presented to the Market Risk Committee
•	Steered a testing initiative for derivative contracts module that optimised trading desk capital allocation by 40%, directly contributing to broader corporate risk management strategies
•	Supervised launch of 15 new FX, interest rate, and commodities derivatives  products from a credit risk perspective, conferring with sales & trading division along with specifying methodology and software requirements
•	Devised and approved risk models, assisted in calculating risk metrics in 30 structured derivative deals for the sales & trading department that generated £12m in net income

headline: Boston Consulting Group (BCG) | Climate & Sustainability
about:
I'm passionate about driving sustainable innovation and helping global organizations tackle the challenges of decarbonization. At Boston Consulting Group (BCG), I collaborate with leading companies—particularly in hard-to-abate sectors like aluminum, steel, and cement—to adopt cutting-edge, low-carbon technologies and set new industry standards in sustainability.

With a Master’s in Sustainability and Social Innovation from HEC Paris, I combine deep academic knowledge with hands-on experience in developing strategies that deliver tangible results. From leading decarbonization efforts in industrial sectors to building emissions abatement strategies for global consumer brands, my work consistently focuses on measurable outcomes that accelerate the path to net-zero.

I’m driven by the belief that overcoming the complex challenges of climate change requires bold collaboration and innovation across industries. My mission is to help organizations make a lasting, positive impact on the global climate by driving forward transformative solutions that pave the way for a more sustainable and resilient future.

experience.description: Member of BCG team supporting the WEF's First Movers Coalition across 7 hard-to-abate industrial sectors.

During my tenure as an Associate at BCG, I worked almost exclusively in the Climate & Sustainability (C&S) practice area with a range of consumer, industrial, and NGO clients. Within C&S, I have experience in scope 1-3 emissions reduction road mapping & modeling, nature target-setting, building the investment case for carbon capture (e.g., leveraging the IRA for BECCS projects), and more.

Bridges for Enterprise (BfE) is a global non-profit providing pro bono advisory services to early-stage social enterprises in the developing world.

As Global Partnerships Manager, I established and maintained formal partnerships for the organization with the aims of ultimately strengthening our incubation program and/or the social entrepreneurship ecosystem. To develop these meaningful partnerships, I worked closely with Growth & Partnership Directors at the regional level (NY, Singapore, and Cambridge).

Led the development of Just Transition KPIs for presentation to the board of Engie Global. This involved benchmarking industry leaders in Just Transition practices, followed by a comprehensive internal review of ongoing and completed projects across multiple business units worldwide. Collaborated closely with the CSR team at Engie’s Paris HQ to deliver a KPI framework, supporting the board’s efforts in shaping Engie’s global Just Transition policies

publications.title: US Higher Education's Make-or-Break Moment
publications.description:
For higher education institutions, the question is no longer whether change is needed, but how fast can institutions make it happen. 
Colleges and universities are facing an existential crisis due to converging pressures from lower enrollments, federal cuts, the emergence of AI, and changing societal expectations.
Fortunately, higher education leaders have an arsenal of powerful levers—technology, agile operational models, and valuable intellectual and brand assets—that can be activated for short-, medium-, and long-term gains.
Institutions that accelerate investment in digital infrastructure, workforce-relevant programming, deeper industry partnerships, and scalable revenue streams can not only safeguard their financial sustainability but also build more resilient, future-ready organizations.

receivedRecommendations.givenAt: February 12, 2015, Perry was Dane’s teacher
receivedRecommendations.description: I met Dane when he was a student in a course I taught: Introduction to Bioinformatics. This course consists of two main components. The first component is a survey of the bioinformatics field. Students are exposed to scientists from many different disciplines (e.g. human genetics, phylogenetics and systematics, botany, developmental biology, etc.) who are bioinformaticists themselves, or whose research would benefit from the use of bioinformatics and computational biology. Students are asked, specifically, to identify ways that bioinformatics could improve their ability to test scientific hypotheses in the labs they work in. In the second component of the class students learn to use regular expressions and are introduced to the Python programming language. This is a very rigorous class and the majority of the students have no prior programming experience; however, they are expected to learn quickly and by the end of the semester students who succeed are able to perform simple manipulations of large VCF files (files used for storing genetic information from next-generation sequencing projects). Dane worked very hard and consistently improved. He demonstrated that he is capable of quickly learning very difficult concepts. I happily recommend Dane and am confident he will be successful in whatever he chooses.

During this time, I demonstrated my motivation, hard work, scientific insight, experimental skills, and data analysis and programming skills. Prior to arriving at Princeton, I studied at Peking University, where I obtained a B.S. in Biological sciences. I worked on neurodegenerative diseases in mouse models, and I also completed a summer research program at the University of Chicago, where I worked on motor neuron terminal differentiation.

publications.title: Male-specific behavioral and transcriptomic changes in aging C. elegans neurons
publications.description:
•Male worms undergo cognitive decline and neuron morphology defects with age
•Male neuron RNA-seq uncovers sexual dimorphism in transcriptomic changes with age
•X chromosome genes have a greater hermaphrodite bias with age
•hrg-7, whose expression declines with age, is required for male sensory behaviors

publications.title: The Neuron-specific IIS/FOXO Transcriptome in Aged Animals Reveals Regulatory Mechanisms of Cognitive Aging
publications.description: Cognitive decline is a significant health concern in our aging society. Here, we used the model organism C. elegans to investigate the impact of the IIS/FOXO pathway on age-related cognitive decline. The daf-2 Insulin/IGF-1 receptor mutant exhibits a significant extension of learning and memory span with age compared to wild-type worms, an effect that is dependent on the DAF-16 transcription factor. To identify possible mechanisms by which aging daf-2 mutants maintain learning and memory with age while wild-type worms lose neuronal function, we carried out neuron-specific transcriptomic analysis in aged animals. We observed downregulation of neuronal genes and upregulation of transcriptional regulation genes in aging wild-type neurons. By contrast, IIS/FOXO pathway mutants exhibit distinct neuronal transcriptomic alterations in response to cognitive aging, including upregulation of stress response genes and downregulation of specific insulin signaling genes. We tested the roles of significantly transcriptionally-changed genes in regulating cognitive functions, identifying novel regulators of learning and memory. In addition to other mechanistic insights, comparison of the aged vs young daf-2 neuronal transcriptome revealed that a new set of potentially neuroprotective genes is upregulated; instead of simply mimicking a young state, daf-2 may enhance neuronal resilience to accumulation of harm and take a more active approach to combat aging. These findings suggest a potential mechanism for regulating cognitive function with age and offer insights into novel therapeutic targets for age-related cognitive decline.

publications.title: Adult Single-nucleus Neuronal Transcriptomes of Insulin Signaling Mutants Reveal Regulators of Behavior and Learning
publications.description: The insulin/insulin-like signaling (IIS) pathway regulates many of C. elegans′ adult functions, including learning and memory1. While whole-worm and tissue-specific transcriptomic analyses have identified IIS targets2,3, a higher-resolution single-cell approach is required to identify changes that confer neuron-specific improvements in the long-lived insulin receptor mutant, daf-2. To understand how behaviors that are controlled by a small number of neurons change in daf-2 mutants, we used the deep resolution of single-nucleus RNA sequencing to define each neuron type′s transcriptome in adult wild-type and daf-2 mutants. First, we found surprising differences between wild-type L4 larval neurons and young adult neurons in chemoreceptor expression, synaptic genes, and learning and memory genes. These Day 1 adult neuron transcriptomes allowed us to identify adult AWC-specific regulators of chemosensory function and to predict neuron-to-neuron peptide/receptor pairs. We then identified gene expression changes that correlate with daf-2′s improved cognitive functions, particularly in the AWC sensory neuron that controls learning and associative memory4, and used behavioral assays to test their roles in cognitive function. Combining deep single-neuron transcriptomics, genetic manipulation, and behavioral analyses enabled us to identify genes that may function in a single adult neuron to control behavior, including conserved genes that function in learning and memory.

publications.title: Male-specific features of C. elegans neuronal aging
publications.description: Aging is a complex biological process, with sexually dimorphic aspects. For example, men and women differ in their vulnerabilities in cognitive decline, suggesting biological sex may contribute to the heterogeneous nature of aging. Although we know a great deal about the cognitive aging of hermaphrodites of the model system C. elegans, less is known about cognitive decline in males. Through behavioral analyses, we found that the cognitive aging process has both sex-shared and sex-dimorphic characteristics. Through neuron-specific sequencing, we identified neuronal age-associated sex-differential targets. In addition to sex-shared neuronal aging genes, males differentially downregulate mitochondrial metabolic genes and upregulate GPCR genes with age. In addition, the X chromosome exhibits increased gene expression in hermaphrodites and altered dosage compensation complex expression with age, indicating possible X-chromosomal dysregulation that contributes to sexual dimorphism in cognitive aging. Finally, we found that the sex-differentially expressed gene hrg-7, which encodes an aspartic-type endopeptidase, regulates male behavior during cognitive aging but does not affect hermaphrodites’ behaviors. Overall, these results suggest that males and hermaphrodites exhibit different age-related neuronal changes. This study will strengthen our understanding of sex-specific vulnerability and resilience and help identify new pathways to target with novel treatments that could benefit both sexes.

publications.title: Neuronal activation of Gaq EGL-30/GNAQ late in life rejuvenates cognition across species
publications.description: Loss of cognitive function with age is devastating. EGL-30/GNAQ and Gaq signaling pathways are highly conserved between C. elegans and mammals, and murine Gnaq is enriched in hippocampal neurons and de- clines with age. We found that activation of EGL-30 in aged worms triples memory span, and GNAQ gain of function significantly improved memory in aged mice: GNAQ(gf) in hippocampal neurons of 24-month-old mice (equivalent to 70- to 80-year-old humans) rescued age-related impairments in well-being and memory. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed increased expression of genes regulating synaptic function, axon guidance, and memory in GNAQ-treated mice, and worm orthologs of these genes were required for long- term memory extension in worms. These experiments demonstrate that C. elegans is a powerful model to identify mammalian regulators of memory, leading to the identification of a pathway that improves memory in extremely old mice. To our knowledge, this is the oldest age at which an intervention has improved age- related cognitive decline.

publications.title: Control of spinal motor neuron terminal differentiation through sustained Hoxc8 gene activity
publications.description: Spinal motor neurons (MNs) constitute cellular substrates for several movement disorders. Although their early development has received much attention, how spinal MNs become and remain terminally differentiated is poorly understood. Here, we determined the transcriptome of mouse MNs located at the brachial domain of the spinal cord at embryonic and postnatal stages. We identified novel transcription factors (TFs) and terminal differentiation genes (e.g. ion channels, neurotransmitter receptors, adhesion molecules) with continuous expression in MNs. Interestingly, genes encoding homeodomain TFs (e.g. HOX, LIM), previously implicated in early MN development, continue to be expressed postnatally, suggesting later functions. To test this idea, we inactivated Hoxc8 at successive stages of mouse MN development and observed motor deficits. Our in vivo findings suggest that Hoxc8 is not only required to establish, but also maintain expression of several MN terminal differentiation markers. Data from in vitro generated MNs indicate Hoxc8 acts directly and is sufficient to induce expression of terminal differentiation genes. Our findings dovetail recent observations in Caenorhabditis elegans MNs, pointing toward an evolutionarily conserved role for Hox in neuronal terminal differentiation.

headline: BCG Associate | UChicago Molecular Engineering Grad
about: I am a BCG associate based in San Diego. I graduated from The University of Chicago in 2025 with a B.S. in Molecular Engineering and a minor in Molecular Engineering for Sustainability and Water Resources. I’m interested in renewable energy developments, and hope to have a positive impact on sustainability as a consultant.

experience.description: The Collaborative Learning in Molecular Engineering (CLIME) program is an official pass/fail class at UChicago. As a problem set writer, I was responsible for writing challenging engineering problems to help students excel in the Molecular Engineering major.

experience.companyName: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering at the University of Chicago
experience.description: As an undergraduate researcher in the Hsu Group at the Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, I conducted electrochemical experiments to aid in our research on reversible electrodeposition for a sustainable future.

The Collaborative Learning in Molecular Engineering (CLIME) program is an official pass/fail class at UChicago. As a team leader, I was responsible for assisting students with challenging engineering problems to help them excel in the Molecular Engineering major.

As a part of the BCG GFL program, I worked as a Summer Associate in the San Diego office. I worked with a team on multiple MedTech cases surrounding topics like proteomics and genomic sequencing. I used client input, conducted interviews with market experts, and performed research using a wide variety of online sources (e.g., academic publications, FDA guidance documents, SEC filings) to generate valuable insights, providing in-depth analyses of various technologies and markets, and developing strategic, actionable plans for companies to succeed in their respective industries.

As a full time lab assistant, I performed analytical procedures and contributed to bioassay testing on water and sediment samples. headline: Product Lead | Innovator and Business Builder
about:
I'm a product leader who loves building things—especially products that solve real problems and create tangible impact.

At BCG X, I partner closely with global clients and multidisciplinary teams to launch and scale digital ventures. That means diving into big, messy problems and turning them into clear strategies and products that customers actually want and use. I've built products from scratch, helped companies find their product-market fit, and scaled solutions across healthtech, fintech, consumer tech, and beyond.

My approach is collaborative and pragmatic. I believe great products come from empowered teams, clear communication, and a genuine curiosity to learn and adapt along the way. I'm at my best navigating ambiguity, aligning diverse stakeholders, and translating complex ideas into practical, actionable plans.

I'm always interested in meeting thoughtful people, learning something new, and talking about what's next in tech, strategy, or just the best new coffee spot. Feel free to reach out!

publications.title: Missionaries Outperform in Venture Funding
publications.publishedAt: International Journal of Entrepreneurship, Vol.26 Iss.5 · Sep 1, 2022
publications.description:
Scientific paper about the impact of founder characteristics and motives on funding performance of new ventures (total amount of funding raised / number of funding rounds closed). Key finding: Founders motivated by the desire to contribute to society & a multi-stakeholder approach (Missionary founder social identity) are more successful in raising funds than those being motivated by economic goals only.


ABSTRACT

While prior research has evidenced the impact of founder social identities on new venture creation, our understanding of how founder identity affects funding performance as a critical determinant for venture success is limited. Given that different identities define various motivational concepts—that is, missionaries increasing benefits for society at large, as opposed to darwinians maximizing economic self-interest and communitarians supporting a particular community—we propose a model for how such founder identity differences relate to ambiguous funding outcomes. 
Our findings reveal that the missionary founder social identity has a significantly positive impact on funding performance. 
We discuss our contributions to founder social identity theory and its intersection with behavioral finance.

I remain deeply curious about the world around me, and this has manifested itself in my career. Reinventing Gender Diversity Programs for a Post-Pandemic World
Why the First Year Matters for LGBTQ+ Employees
publications.description: The first year of employment is critical for LGBTQ+ employees, with 70% coming out then or likely not at all. This has major implications for companies, as employees who feel comfortable sharing their identity at work report feeling more empowered, more comfortable about speaking up, being themselves, and building close friendships at work. Our survey of ~ 8,800 people in 19 countries also shed light on the challenges that trans and gender nonconforming (TGNC) employees and LBTQ+ women face when making choices about being out at work. For instance, 74% of TGNC respondents reported instances of discrimination versus 57% of LGBQ+ respondents. And LBTQ+ women who are out reported a 13% greater incidence of sexual harassment than did their male counterparts. The article outlines 5 concrete areas, across the employee lifecycle, that companies can address to encourage employees to be out.

headline: Senior Global Health Expert | Ecosystem Catalyst | Problem Solver | Board Chair |
topSkills: Strategic Planning • Analysis • Program Evaluation • Research • Program Management
about:
With over 17 years of experience covering all aspects of Global Health, I am a PPL at Boston Consulting Group (BCG), where I apply my expertise in global and public health, universal health coverage, primary healthcare, and community health systems to solve complex challenges and create social impact. I  hold an MA in International Development & Policy from the University of Chicago, an MBA from MIT, an MPA from Harvard Kennedy School, and undergraduate degrees from the University of Pennsylvania.

I have served as Senior Advisor to Cabinet Ministers in multiple governments to advance their ambitious strategic health plans. In Kenya, I was Senior Advisor to the Cabinet Secretary for Health working with with the Office of the President on Universal Health Coverage advancing to the President's Big 4 Agenda. 

Tapping into the entrepreneurial ecosystems at MIT and Harvard; I am an Advisor at HER Heard, a start-up that amplifies the voices of women, and a founder of This Generation Now and the African Century VC-Impact Fund, two initiatives that aim to empower and mobilize young African leaders and innovators in the health sector.

As a clinician, an entrepreneur, a private and VC investor, a high-impact consultant, and a board chair, I have a multidimensional perspective and a passion for driving positive change in the health sector and beyond. I have worked with diverse stakeholders, including governments, nonprofits, and private sector partners, to design and implement innovative solutions and strategies that improve health outcomes and access in Africa and other regions.

All-in-all, I have raised and deployed nearly $1 billion from multi-laterals, foundations, and governments to other governments and programs so that they can strengthen public health systems, reach marginalized communities, and enhance life-saving access for tens of millions.
